what: VICI Properties owns the land and buildings under casinos and entertainment venues, including Caesars Palace, the Venetian and MGM Grand on the Las Vegas Strip. The operators run the businesses and pay rent on very long leases.
customers: Casino and entertainment operators such as Caesars, MGM Resorts and Penn Entertainment, plus bowling and golf operators.
money: triple-net leases on 93 gaming and experiential properties
moat: Irreplaceable real estate on the Las Vegas Strip under leases of thirty years or more with rent increases built in, where the tenant cannot move the business elsewhere.
risks: Tenant concentration: Caesars and MGM account for most of its rent
Casino operators' fortunes determine whether rent is comfortably covered
Rising interest rates raise its refinancing costs
opportunities: Operating margin of 91% and net margin of 69%, because a triple-net landlord has almost no costs
A dividend yield above 7% backed by contracted rent
Most leases have rent increases tied to inflation
watch: Rent coverage ratios at its largest tenants and new acquisitions.
